summary: Martin Cook describes a new OptionsFunc property he added to the RenderMudSelectAttribute and RenderMudSelect-related attributes in his CG.Blazor.Forms._MudBlazor NuGet package. The property lets a MudSelect dropdown be populated at runtime from a named method on the view-model, instead of only a static comma-separated Options list. The article walks through the attribute's source, including ToAttributes, Generate, and the TryOptionsFunc reflection lookup that compiles the method into a callable func.
one_line: Explains the OptionsFunc property that lets a MudSelect dropdown in CG.Blazor.Forms._MudBlazor be populated from a view-model method at runtime.
key_facts: Martin Cook added a property called OptionsFunc to the MudSelectAttribute and MudRadioGroupAttribute attributes in his CG.Blazor.Forms._MudBlazor NuGet package.
The article posted November 21, 2021 focuses on the RenderMudSelectAttribute class.
The example view-model ExampleVM has a property Foo decorated with [RenderMudSelect(OptionsFunc = "GetOptions")].
The GetOptions method in the example takes no parameters and returns Task<IEnumerable<string>> with the values "Item A" and "Item B".
The Options property can be set to a comma separated list of hard coded options for a static list.
RenderMudSelectAttribute derives from MudBlazorAttribute, which derives from FormGeneratorAttribute.
The ToAttributes method wraps non-default property values into a dictionary to pass to the MudSelect component, and deliberately does not add the options.
The Generate method only renders a MudSelect when the property type is string; otherwise it logs a debug message and skips rendering.
Generate sets Label to the property name when no label is specified, and sets the T attribute to the string type name.
TryOptionsFunc searches for the named method first on the view-model and then on the property parent (model), using public, non-public and instance binding flags.
If the OptionsFunc method is not found or the property is empty, Generate falls back to splitting the Options property on commas.
Each option is rendered as a MudSelectItem<string> child component inside the MudSelect.
Martin Cook says he has yet to add OptionsFunc to the equivalent HTML attributes and intends to also add it to the Syncfusion attributes where applicable.
The article's author is Martin Cook, who has been working with computers professionally since the late 1980s.
